summary: Stateless FastAPI service over a relational store: a create path, a hot redirect path that records clicks best-effort, and an analytics read path, with health, readiness, metrics and rate limiting built in.
components: Observability middleware (request id, JSON access log, Prometheus metrics and latency histogram)
Golden signals and SLO evaluation (/ops/golden-signals, live /ops/dashboard)

endpoints.purpose: Create a short URL (optional alias, expiry, max_clicks)
302 redirect and record a click; 404 unknown, 410 expired or exhausted
Latency, traffic, errors, saturation and SLO status

decisions.rationale: 62^7 ~ 3.5e12 space, no coordination between replicas, unguessable
decisions.alternative: Counter + base62 (predictable, needs a coordinated sequence) or URL hash (collision/dedupe semantics)

decisions.decision: Insert relying on the UNIQUE constraint, retry on conflict
decisions.rationale: Race-safe; check-then-insert has a TOCTOU window
Every hit reaches the service, so analytics stay accurate
decisions.alternative: 301 (cacheable and faster, but hides repeat hits)

decisions.rationale: A failed click write is metered and logged but never fails the redirect

decisions.decision: SQLite for the prototype, PostgreSQL for production
decisions.rationale: Zero-setup demo; SQLAlchemy makes it a DATABASE_URL change

decisions.decision: Domain errors in the service layer, mapped to HTTP at the edge
decisions.rationale: Business logic testable without the web framework

decisions.decision: Atomic conditional UPDATE for the click limit
decisions.rationale: One statement both checks and consumes, so parallel redirects cannot overshoot
decisions.alternative: Read count then write (races) or SELECT ... FOR UPDATE (row lock, not portable to SQLite)

tradeoffs: Analytics consistency vs redirect availability: availability wins
Synchronous click writes (simple) vs queued writes (throughput): simple for the prototype
In-memory rate limiter is per-process: correct for one replica; use Redis or the gateway for many
Random codes need collision retries; counters would not, but they couple replicas
scaling_path: Scale API replicas behind a load balancer
PostgreSQL with read replicas and PgBouncer
Redis read-through cache for hot code -> URL
Queue + batch writer for clicks; time-partitioned clicks table
